hybrid_bridge_pool.translated_query: भौतिक संपत्ति स्थायी सुख क्यों नहीं देती?

answer.answer: Material wealth does not provide lasting happiness because the fulfillment of desires through material objects is only temporary and leads to the emergence of new, stronger desires. This cycle of desire and temporary satisfaction causes continuous misery, as happiness experienced upon attainment is fleeting and soon replaced by sorrow or greed for more. Even if all material possessions were acquired, desire would continue to increase, making permanent satisfaction impossible. Additionally, the happiness derived from material objects is not universal or permanent; it varies from person to person and is often followed by anxiety, fear of loss, or suffering. True and lasting happiness can only be attained by realizing God, as material progress and possessions cannot purify the inner self or bring inner peace [1][2][3][4][5][6][7][8].

answer.answer: भौतिक धन से स्थायी सुख इसलिए नहीं मिलता क्योंकि इच्छाएँ कभी समाप्त नहीं होतीं; एक इच्छा पूरी होने पर दूसरी और अधिक तीव्र इच्छा उत्पन्न हो जाती है। जैसे एक भिखारी ₹1 चाहता है और उसे मिल जाने पर आराम से सो जाता है, वैसे ही करोड़पति बनने के बाद अरबपति बनने की इच्छा होती है, और यह क्रम चलता रहता है। इस प्रकार, भौतिक वस्तुओं की प्राप्ति से जो सुख मिलता है वह क्षणिक होता है और उसके बाद फिर दुःख या नई इच्छाएँ उत्पन्न होती हैं। इसके अलावा, भौतिक वस्तुओं की प्राप्ति के पहले, दौरान और बाद में दुःख और चिंता बनी रहती है, जैसे बच्चे की माँ को बच्चे की चिंता सताती रहती है। इसलिए, भौतिक धन से स्थायी सुख प्राप्त नहीं हो सकता क्योंकि इच्छाओं का अंत नहीं होता और सुख अस्थायी होता है[1][2][3][7][8]।

hybrid_bridge_pool.translated_query: Why does permanent happiness not come from paisa (money) and dhan (wealth)?

answer.answer: Paisa aur dhan se permanent sukh isliye nahi milta kyunki jab koi ichha puri hoti hai, to uske turant baad aur adhik lobh ya ichha utpann hoti hai. Is tarah ichha kabhi khatam nahi hoti, aur har ichha ke poori hone par ya na poori hone par dukh ya krodh hota hai. Isliye sukh sthayi nahi hota, balki pal bhar ka hota hai jo turant kisi naye dukh ya chinta mein badal jata hai. Jaise ki koi vyakti jo ek lakh ka malik tha, wo crore pati banne ki ichha karta hai, aur crore pati banne ke baad arabpati banne ki ichha hoti hai. Is prakriya mein sukh kabhi sthayi nahi hota. Yeh sab isliye hota hai kyunki vasna aur lobh ka ant nahi hota. Isliye paisa aur dhan se kabhi permanent sukh nahi mil sakta [1][2][3][7][8].

answer.answer: Devotion should begin in childhood because it is easier to develop a sincere attachment to God at a young age without the distractions and attachments that come with adulthood. For example, the story of Prahlad shows that even a child can be deeply devoted to God, and this early devotion helps in practicing bhakti without the interference of worldly desires or attachments. Children can engage in devotion sincerely while still performing their worldly duties without attachment, as Prahlad did [1][4]. Starting devotion early helps cultivate a pure and focused mind, which is essential for true bhakti [3].

Regarding wealth, the lecture explains that people continuously desire more wealth, never feeling satisfied.
